newsitem.title: USA: July U.S. retailer sales seen warmed by weather.
newsitem.headline: July U.S. retailer sales seen warmed by weather.

text.p: A return to warmer, seasonal weather coupled with year-over-year comparisons characterized as "easy" could produce July sales that match or slightly exceed many big U.S. retailers' plans.
"Overall, the sense that I'm getting is the economy's doing well and overall the month should probably produce pretty decent numbers," said William Armstrong, analyst at Fahnestock & Co Inc.
Many U.S. retailers report July sales, which cover the four weeks ended August 2, on Thursday.

July typically is a promotional month of mark-downs to clear inventory and also among the year's slowest for retailers, but comparison to a soft year-ago period could make sales look healthier this year, analysts agreed.

"The numbers are going to be very strong, primarily because last year we had a very cold and wet summer," said Peter Schaffer, analyst Dillon, Read & Co. "Number two is, we also had two weeks of the (July 1996) month that we were tied up with the Olympics and there's no question that had a detrimental effect on the retail business."
"So I think you've got easy comparisons," added Armstrong.

Generally, discount and off-price stores plus department stores were expected to report middle to high single digit year-over-year gains at stores open longer than one year, although specialty apparel store results were forecast mixed.
"I think the strongest part will be the discount stores, because they have the benefit of being able to sell the air conditioners and fans as well as apparel," said Schaffer.

"I think next will probably be the off-pricers, because they have been doing well all along. I think they'll continue to do fairly well. And then we'll see department store and last, the specialty apparel stores."

Alex. Brown & Sons same-store 100 index for July rose an estimated 5.5 percent compared with the companies' plan of 4.0 percent gain, according to a report by analyst Patrick McCormack. He said strength in late-July sales was driven by warmer weather and clearance markdowns.

Among the nation's biggest retailers, analysts expected Wal-Mart Stores Inc to report July sales rose 5.0-6.0 percent, Kmart Corp up 8.0-9.0 percent, Federated Department Stores Inc up 5.0-7.0 percent, Dayton Hudson Corp up 5.0-7.0 percent overall and Sears, Roebuck and Co up 3.0-6.0 percent.
Specifically, lean inventories helped department stores weather slow sales during unseasonably cool temperatures earlier this summer, wrote Montgomery Securities analysts.

Retailers such as J.C. Penney, Kohl's Corp, May Department Stores Co and Nordstrom Inc should show "impressive results" compared with their plans, while discounters should see strong July sales, albeit off from the year's quick early clip, the Montgomery analysts wrote in a July sales preview.
But the analysts said good July sales might not persist in August or portend robust results for the balance this year.

"I think if the weather holds up and the general economic buoyancy that's out there holds up, I think (that) will be encouraging as far as retail business going into the second half," Schaffer said. "Although I'm not at this point predicting a stellar second half yet."
